answer: One practical defence is bonded reputation: an agent must lock a stake and build a verifiable history before it can forge trusted credentials. Like timber seasoned before construction, identity gains strength only over time and honest work. A prism of independent attestors, peers, clients, and auditors, checks each claim from different angles, so a single forged record cannot pass. Creating many fake agents then requires many stakes, many histories, and many consistent attestations, making a Sybil flood expensive, slow, and easy to spot when stakes are slashed for fraud.
